summary: Go through the text once: skip anything that is not a letter, then sort each letter into vowel or consonant (T3 — string classification). Lowercasing first means we only need to check five vowels.

blocks.title: Read the text
blocks.text: A plain `input()` — the text may contain spaces, digits and symbols.

blocks.title: Two counters
blocks.text: Both start at 0, so text with no letters at all prints 0 and 0.

blocks.title: Only letters count
blocks.text: `s.lower()` makes `'A'` and `'a'` the same. `ch.isalpha()` skips digits, spaces and symbols — without it, `'1'` and `'!'` would be counted as consonants.

blocks.title: Vowel or consonant?
blocks.text: A letter is either in `"aeiou"` or it is a consonant. `y` is not in the string, so it counts as a consonant, as the problem says.

blocks.title: Print two lines
blocks.text: Two separate `print` calls give `Vowels: V` and `Consonants: C` on their own lines.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 1000 characters — instant.
pitfalls: Counting digits or symbols as consonants (no `isalpha()` check).
